To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a culturing system for the study of AMD microbial communities and used quantitative proteomics to verify that the laboratory-grown communities are similar to natural AMD communities.

we developed an experimental system for laboratory cultivation of natural AMD microbial communities, and we used quantitative proteomics to demonstrate that the cultivated communities were similar to natural communities at the functional level, and to identify factors limiting laboratory cultivation.

we have developed a culturing system that can support dense acid mine drainage microbial communities and that a comprehensive proteomic analysis of these communities has revealed the presence of active low abundance bacteria and Archaea that have not been cultivated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cultivation of complex microbial communities and the development of quantitative proteomic methods to analyze them.
the cultivation and proteomic analysis of AMD biofilm communities.
the cultivation of acidophilic biofilm communities from AMD habitats and with the development and application of a metabolic labelling-based quantitative proteomic method to study these communities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the laboratory system is a good model for natural communities.
the research presented here resulted in a model system ideal for testing ecological and physiological hypotheses.
the laboratory system is a good model of the natural communities and is useful in the study of the ecology and physiology of acidophilic biofilm communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of a quantitative proteomic analysis of microbial communities has enabled the design of an ideal system for studying the ecology of AMD biofilms.

we have shown that a quantitative proteomic approach can be successfully applied to the analysis of a model microbial community, and that this approach has provided new insight into the physiology and ecology of these communities.

the application of quantitative proteomics to a model AMD microbial community enabled the development of a reproducible, scalable laboratory model system that can be used for testing ecological and physiological hypotheses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cultivation of microbial communities can be achieved and the resulting communities can be studied at the functional level using quantitative proteomic approaches.
the application of quantitative proteomics to the study of microbial communities is a powerful approach to understanding the functional properties of complex communities.

the metabolic labeling-based quantitative approach is a valuable tool for the characterization of complex microbial communities, and that laboratory-grown communities can be used to test hypotheses about the ecology of natural communities.
